Confirms the three reason variants. I have everything needed.

## NPU power/clock state

**Mechanism** (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py`): reads amdxdna's debugfs nodes at `/sys/kernel/debug/accel/<bdf>/{dpm_level,powerstate}` — an optional, best-effort corroborating signal, *not* the primary NPU activity source (XRT submission-counter deltas remain primary, per the module docstring at `src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:1-9`).

- `read_npu_power()` (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:96`) resolves the per-device debugfs dir via `_debugfs_dir()` (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:39`), which picks the dir matching a given BDF or, if none given, the first sorted subdir of `DEBUGFS_ACCEL` (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:30,54-57`).
- It reads `dpm_level` (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:118`) and parses it with `parse_dpm_level()` (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:70`), extracting the `[bracketed]` active `npuclk,hclk` token via regex `_DPM_TOKEN` (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:36`), plus the raw `powerstate` string (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:119`).

**Return shape**: always a dict with keys `available`, `source`, `reason`, `powerstate`, `dpm` (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:105-111`). `available` is `False` unless it reaches the final assignment (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:133-136`).

**Distinct unavailability reasons** (`reason` field, all confirmed by `tests/test_npu_power.py:38-125`):

| reason | condition | where set |
|---|---|---|
| `debugfs_accel_absent` | no accel dir for the requested BDF, no accel dirs at all, or an `OSError` while listing (root-only `/sys/kernel/debug`, not mounted, driver doesn't export it) | `_debugfs_dir` returns `None` → `src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:113-116` |
| `debugfs_nodes_unreadable` | dir exists but **both** `dpm_level` and `powerstate` fail to read (`OSError` in `_read`, e.g. permission denied) | `src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:120-124` |
| `debugfs_nodes_unparsable` | at least one node read, but `dpm_level` had no parseable `npuclk,hclk` token *and* `powerstate` was empty | `src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:126-131` |

Note `_read()` (`src/xdna_top/npu_power.py:62-67`) itself returns `None` on any `OSError`, never raising — that's the low-level "can't read this file" signal, distinct from the three higher-level `reason` strings above which are what callers actually see.

## iGPU telemetry discovery

Entirely separate module/mechanism: `discover_sysfs()` in `src/xdna_top/discover_sysfs.py:8`. No debugfs, no ioctl — pure sysfs probing, run-to-completion (no BDF targeting).

- **Busy %**: hard-coded candidate list `/sys/class/drm/card{0,1,2}/device/gpu_busy_percent` (`src/xdna_top/discover_sysfs.py:22-26`). Iterates in that fixed order, picks the **first** that exists and is readable, sets `status = "iGPU found"`, then `break`s — earliest card index wins, no further comparison (`src/xdna_top/discover_sysfs.py:27-36`).
- **Power**: walks every entry under `/sys/class/hwmon/` (`src/xdna_top/discover_sysfs.py:39-41`), and for each dir with a readable `power1_input`, reads its `name` file too (`src/xdna_top/discover_sysfs.py:42-52`). Selection rule: `if name == "amdgpu" or not result["gpu_power_path"]` (`src/xdna_top/discover_sysfs.py:55-56`) — i.e. it keeps overwriting `gpu_power_path` with whatever hwmon it finds until one is named `amdgpu`, which always wins and short-circuits further overwrites; a non-`amdgpu` hwmon only sticks if no `amdgpu` one is ever seen.
- If nothing is found, `status` stays at its initial value `"CPU-only fallback"` (`src/xdna_top/discover_sysfs.py:18`), and both path fields remain `None`.

One correctness note worth flagging: the hwmon loop has no `break` after matching `amdgpu`, so it keeps scanning remaining hwmon dirs; if a *later* non-`amdgpu` hwmon is also found after an `amdgpu` one was already set, the `or not result["gpu_power_path"]` branch is false (path is already set) so it's safe — but only because `name == "amdgpu"` is checked first each iteration, not because of any lock-in once amdgpu is found. Functionally correct, just worth knowing it doesn't short-circuit the directory walk.

## Recorder (`src/xdna_top/record.py`)

**Event identity**: every JSONL line is a dict with a `"type"` field (`"telemetry"`, `"mark"`, `"meta"`, or `"summary"`) plus a `"schema_version"` (`RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.0"`, `src/xdna_top/record.py:22`). Telemetry/mark/meta/summary events are built by `build_telemetry_event` (`src/xdna_top/record.py:26-36`), `build_mark_event` (`src/xdna_top/record.py:39-46`), `_meta_event` (`src/xdna_top/record.py:171-179`), and `_summary_event` (`src/xdna_top/record.py:182-190`) respectively — that `type` tag is what lets downstream tooling (e.g. `xdna-top assert`) dispatch on event kind.

**Line writing**: `_open_writer` (`src/xdna_top/record.py:197-223`) yields a `write_line` closure — either writing to stdout or opening the output file once in `"w"` mode and appending. Each call does `handle.write(_dump(event)); handle.flush()` (`src/xdna_top/record.py:219-221`), where `_dump` is `json.dumps(event) + "\n"` (`src/xdna_top/record.py:226-227`). Flushing per line is deliberate (see docstring `src/xdna_top/record.py:201-204`) so an interrupted recording still leaves a valid, tail-able partial file. `run_record` (`src/xdna_top/record.py:114-155`) drives the sequence: write one `meta` event, then loop via `record_stream` writing one `telemetry` event per sample, then write one trailing `summary` event.

## Exporter (`src/xdna_top/exporter.py`)

**Wiring to the registry**: `serve()` (`src/xdna_top/exporter.py:103-109`) creates a fresh `CollectorRegistry()` and registers `XdnaCollector` (`src/xdna_top/exporter.py:128-152`), which wraps a `read_fn` closure built by `_hardware_reader` (`src/xdna_top/exporter.py:92-100`) that samples the `HardwareGauge` and reads NPU power at scrape time. `XdnaCollector.collect()` (`src/xdna_top/exporter.py:142-151`) is what `prometheus_client`'s HTTP server calls on every scrape — it delegates to `_build_metrics` (`src/xdna_top/exporter.py:20-89`), which yields `GaugeMetricFamily`/`CounterMetricFamily` instances. This is stateless/pull-based by design (docstring `src/xdna_top/exporter.py:3-6`): no background sampling loop, Prometheus owns history.

**Naming rule**: counter families must be registered **without** the `_total` suffix — `prometheus_client` appends it automatically. That's called out explicitly in the comment at `src/xdna_top/exporter.py:62`, right above `xdna_npu_submissions`/`xdna_npu_completions` (`src/xdna_top/exporter.py:63-70`), which become `xdna_npu_submissions_total` / `xdna_npu_completions_total` on the wire. If you add a new counter metric and include `_total` yourself, `prometheus_client` will double it up — keep the bare name for `CounterMetricFamily`, and only gauges (`GaugeMetricFamily`, e.g. `xdna_up` at `src/xdna_top/exporter.py:31-33`) get their literal name as-is.

`channel/enroll.sh` owns enrollment. It writes three files, all under `/etc` and `/usr/share`:

- **Keyring**: `/usr/share/keyrings/fde-station-archive-keyring.gpg`, mode `0644` — installed via `install -D -m 0644` at `channel/enroll.sh:59` (local copy) or `channel/enroll.sh:65` (fetched from the channel).
- **Apt source**: `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/fde-station.sources`, deb822 format, written at `channel/enroll.sh:80-89`.
- **Credential file**: `/etc/apt/auth.conf.d/fde-station.conf`, mode **`0600`** — created at `channel/enroll.sh:93` (`install -D -m 0600 /dev/null "$AUTH_DEST"`), written under `umask 077` (`channel/enroll.sh:94-97`), then re-asserted with an explicit `chmod 600 "$AUTH_DEST"` at `channel/enroll.sh:98`. It's created empty at the restrictive perms *before* the secret is written, so the PAT is never briefly world/group-readable.

**How the source ties to the keyring**: the deb822 stanza written at `channel/enroll.sh:81-89` includes `Signed-By: $KEYRING_DEST`, i.e. `Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/fde-station-archive-keyring.gpg` — pointing apt at the exact keyring file installed in step 1, so the pinned `URIs: $RAW/$SHA/` source is verified against that key rather than any system-wide trusted keyring.

The credential file itself scopes the PAT to the repo path (`channel/enroll.sh:96`: `machine raw.githubusercontent.com/${REPO_SLUG} login ${LOGIN} password ${PAT}`), so even though it's readable only by root (0600), the auth line is also constrained to `raw.githubusercontent.com/namastex888/fde-station-apt`.
